name: AD Recycle Bin - Restore Deleted Objects
description: When the AD Recycle Bin feature is enabled and you have sufficient privileges, you can enumerate and restore deleted AD objects (users, groups, computers). A deleted privileged account (like a cert_admin) can be restored to regain its original group memberships and permissions - an attacker who controls an account with Restore-ADObject rights can bring back a deleted admin.
notes:
=== THE IDEA ===
AD Recycle Bin keeps deleted objects in a recoverable state (default 180 days).
If a privileged account was deleted (e.g. cert_admin), restoring it recovers
the account WITH its original SID, group memberships, and ACLs.

=== ENUMERATE DELETED OBJECTS ===
  Get-ADObject -Filter 'isDeleted -eq $true' -IncludeDeletedObjects -Properties cn,objectSid,isDeleted

=== FIND A SPECIFIC DELETED USER ===
  Get-ADObject -Filter 'isDeleted -eq $true -and name -like "cert_admin*"' -IncludeDeletedObjects -Properties objectGUID,objectSid,lastKnownParent

=== RESTORE THE OBJECT ===
  Restore-ADObject -Identity '<objectGUID>'
  # e.g. Restore-ADObject -Identity '938182c3-bf0b-410a-9aaa-45c8e1a02ebf'

=== RESET PASSWORD (account is restored but password is unknown) ===
  Set-ADAccountPassword -Identity 'cert_admin' -Reset -NewPassword (ConvertTo-SecureString 'NewPassword123!' -AsPlainText -Force)
  # or from Linux:
  bloodyAD --host <dc_ip> -d <domain> -u <user> -p <password> set password cert_admin 'NewPassword123'

=== CHECK IF RECYCLE BIN IS ENABLED ===
  Get-ADOptionalFeature 'Recycle Bin Feature' | Select EnabledScopes
  # Empty EnabledScopes = NOT enabled

=== NOTES ===
- Multiple deleted objects with the same name get unique GUIDs - pick the right one
- lastKnownParent shows the OU the object was in before deletion
- Restored objects keep their original SID and group memberships

examples.label: Find specific deleted user by name
Restore a deleted object by GUID

recommended.note: After restoring the account, you may need dacledit to grant it enrollment rights on ADCS templates.
A restored cert_admin can enroll in vulnerable certificate templates.

defense.why_it_works: AD Recycle Bin preserves deleted objects with all attributes for a tombstone lifetime (default 180 days). Any principal with the right to restore deleted objects can bring back privileged accounts, inheriting their original SID and group memberships.
defense.prerequisites: AD Recycle Bin must be enabled; the attacker needs delegated rights to Restore-ADObject (or Domain Admin).
defense.impact: Recovery of deleted privileged accounts with their original permissions, bypassing the deletion as a security control.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1098] Event 4662 with Restore access on isDeleted objects; Event 5136 for attribute changes on restored objects.
defense.artifacts: 4662 restore events; newly active accounts that were previously in the Deleted Objects container.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4662
| where AccessMask="0x100" AND ObjectType contains "Deleted"
| table _time, SubjectUserName, ObjectName
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4662
| where ObjectType contains "Deleted" or ObjectName contains "DEL:"
| project TimeGenerated, Actor=SubjectUserName, Target=ObjectName
defense.prevention: Restrict Restore-ADObject delegation; monitor for objects leaving the Deleted Objects container; alert on password resets immediately following object restoration.

detections.name: AD Recycle Bin object restoration
detections.logic:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID in (4662, 5136)
| where ObjectName contains "DEL:" or ObjectName contains "Deleted Objects"
| project TimeGenerated, Actor=SubjectUserName, Target=ObjectName, EventID
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
detections.false_positives: Legitimate disaster recovery restoring accidentally deleted accounts
detections.tuning: Alert specifically on restoration of accounts with adminCount=1 or membership in privileged groups
